=== CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===
- tests/test_unblock_scan.py:958-960 | severity=low | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5, minimax_minimax-m3, z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  PROBLEM: The new test `test_wedged_queued_run_stays_ignored_under_a_long_inflight_window` is followed by only one blank line before `def test_zombie_filter_can_be_disabled(monkeypatch) -> None:`, where two are expected, so ruff raises E302/E305.
  WHY: Nothing fails at runtime, but the pre-push gate runs `ruff check --select E,F` on changed files and would flag this line; earlier rounds of this PR fixed the same E303/E305 gaps in other test files (all three reviewers rated it NIT, and minimax gave it as a hardening suggestion with HARDENING_RISK_SCORE 1).
- scripts/orchestrate_lib.py:567 | severity=high | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite]
  PROBLEM: `is_wedged_queued_run` does not guard against exceptions (e.g., from `_zombie_run_created_epoch`) when it is called inside the `build_concurrency_snapshot` loop.
  WHY: An exception raised on malformed run data would crash the whole concurrency snapshot build, and the poller could not work out run concurrency (gemini rated it MAJOR; anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5 and z-ai_glm-5_3-flash disputed it, saying every input is isinstance-guarded and `_parse_iso8601_to_epoch` (lines 2494-2513) catches ValueError/TypeError/OverflowError/OSError).
- scripts/orchestrate_lib.py:574 | severity=low | confidence=3
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite]
  PROBLEM: `_zombie_run_created_epoch` parses timestamps more strictly than the Bash `zombie_queued_jq_def`, because it requires a "Z" suffix.
  WHY: Drift between the Bash and Python filters could make different guards see different sets of "active" runs (anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5 and z-ai_glm-5_3-flash disputed it, saying the parity is intentional and covered by tests).
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:18437 | severity=low | confidence=3
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite]
  PROBLEM: The temp file that `mktemp` creates in `prime_phase_concurrency_snapshot` is not guaranteed to be cleaned up on every failure path.
  WHY: If the command fails or is interrupted before `rm -f "${caps_err_file}"` runs, the temp file stays behind and small files leak across poller ticks (anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5 disputed it, saying the builder call sits inside `if !`, so `set -e` cannot exit before cleanup).
=== END CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===
